name: Astera Labs
thesis: Astera Labs sells PCIe, CXL and Ethernet connectivity silicon for AI racks; Q2 revenue was $392M (+105% y/y) and Q3 guidance is EPS $1.16-1.21 on consensus revenue of about $551M. Wednesday Oct 14 it fell 7.72% to $300.28, closing near the day's low of $299.19, as hot US CPI (3.7% vs 3.6% expected) hit AI-infrastructure names; no company news found. It is 21.4% below the Oct 7 close of $382.25. TSMC (Oct 15) beat on Q3 (revenue $46.72B vs a $44.6-45.8B guide, HPC 68% of revenue, +22% q/q) and guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B vs about $48.8B expected; 2026 capex stays $60-64B as far as reported (Q3 spend $13.84B, $40.64B year to date), which supports AI-rack connectivity demand into year-end. Consensus target $391.77 (26 analysts, Buy), 30% upside.
risks: Trades at a high multiple with a five-year beta near 3.8: it has now fallen 5-10% on three separate macro or sector scares in six sessions (OpenAI revenue, CXMT memory, CPI). Two Hold-side calls in a month (Susquehanna $310, Northland downgrade); the price is now below Susquehanna's $310. Hyperscaler capex and the Scorpio switch ramp need to keep landing to hold the multiple.
catalyst: Lam Research Oct 21 (08:00 AEDT Thu Oct 22); Q3 results Nov 3 after US close, call 4:30pm ET (08:30 AEDT Wed Nov 4).

name: Broadcom
thesis: Broadcom supplies custom AI accelerators (Google, Meta, OpenAI's Jalapeno) plus Ethernet networking and VMware software. The WSJ reported Oct 7 that it is lining up $50B+ of financing so OpenAI can buy its chips. Wednesday Oct 14 it fell 3.10% to $346.25 in the CPI-driven tech selloff (Nasdaq -1.9%), a smaller drop than the 6-10% losses in the smaller AI-infrastructure names; no Broadcom-specific news found. TSMC (Oct 15) beat on Q3 (revenue $46.72B vs a $44.6-45.8B guide, HPC 68% of revenue, +22% q/q) and guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B vs about $48.8B expected; 2026 capex stays $60-64B as far as reported (Q3 spend $13.84B, $40.64B year to date); HPC, where custom ASICs sit, is now 68% of TSMC revenue. Consensus target $531.31 (50 analysts, Strong Buy), 53% upside.
risks: Broadcom is becoming OpenAI's lender as well as its supplier, so a funding stumble at OpenAI would hit both revenue and credit; the FT reported Oct 14 that Anthropic's growth slowed in Q3, a reminder that AI-lab revenue is not a straight line. Custom accelerators carry lower margins than merchant silicon. Long yields above 5% raise the cost of the AI debt build-out.
catalyst: OpenAI financing terms (unconfirmed by either company); Q4 FY26 results around Dec 10 (not yet confirmed).

name: Celestica
thesis: Celestica designs and builds 800G/1.6T networking switches, servers and storage for hyperscalers. Q2 2026 revenue was $4.70B (+62% y/y); it guided Q3 to $5.25-5.55B revenue and adjusted EPS $2.88-3.08, and raised 2026 to $20.5B revenue (+65%) and $11.30 adjusted EPS (+87%). Wednesday Oct 14 it fell 9.55% to $323.32, giving back Tuesday's gain, in the CPI-driven AI-hardware selloff; no company news found. Q3 results are confirmed for Mon Oct 26 after close, with the call and an Investor and Analyst Day on Tue Oct 27. Mean target $473.91 (22 analysts, Strong Buy) implies 47% upside; the lowest target ($375) is 16% above the price.
risks: Hardware margins are single-digit and a few hyperscalers set the pace; it has now had three 6%+ down days in a week on sector headlines. Competition from Arista, Accton and in-house hyperscaler designs. A 2027 capex digestion year is the bear case, and the investor day will be judged on 2027 targets.
catalyst: Q3 results Mon Oct 26 after US close (about 07:00 AEDT Tue Oct 27); call and Investor and Analyst Day Tue Oct 27, 8:00am ET (23:00 AEDT Tue Oct 27), per company release.

name: Credo Technology
thesis: Credo sells active electrical cables, optical DSPs and PCIe/Ethernet retimers that connect GPUs and switches inside AI data centres. Fiscal Q1 2027 (to Aug 1) revenue was $479M, up 115% year on year, gross margin 64.5%, net income $129M; consensus has FY27 revenue +87% to about $2.5B. Wednesday Oct 14 it fell 9.62% to $179.23, the worst of the watchlist and a fourth straight decline, after trading as low as $179.00; no company news found. TSMC (Oct 15) beat on Q3 (revenue $46.72B vs a $44.6-45.8B guide, HPC 68% of revenue, +22% q/q) and guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B vs about $48.8B expected; 2026 capex stays $60-64B as far as reported (Q3 spend $13.84B, $40.64B year to date). Mean target $279.09 (20 analysts, Strong Buy) implies 56% upside; the price is now 3% below the lowest target ($185).
risks: Customer concentration is high - a handful of hyperscalers drive most revenue, so a design loss or capex pause shows up in a single quarter. Growth is decelerating (272% to 115% over four quarters). The stock swings hardest of the group on sector days (-7.25% Oct 12, -9.62% Oct 14). Competition from Marvell and Broadcom plus any copper-to-optical shift are live threats.
catalyst: Lam Research Oct 21 (08:00 AEDT Thu Oct 22) and hyperscaler capex updates in late-October earnings; fiscal Q2 2027 results early December (date not announced).

name: SK hynix ADR
thesis: SK hynix is the leading HBM supplier to Nvidia and the number-two DRAM maker; the Nasdaq ADR listed in July. The ADR fell 6.06% Wednesday Oct 14 to $147.55, a fourth straight loss and 24.4% below the Oct 2 close of $195.13. Seoul then fell harder on Thursday Oct 15: SK hynix closed at 1,262,000 won (-11.06%), with the KOSPI hitting a circuit breaker at 12:38 KST and Samsung down about 10%, as the US CPI-led tech selloff landed on top of the CXMT DRAM worry. That Seoul close has not yet been priced into the ADR, which trades from 00:30 AEDT Fri. TSMC (Oct 15) beat on Q3 (revenue $46.72B vs a $44.6-45.8B guide, HPC 68% of revenue, +22% q/q) and guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B vs about $48.8B expected; 2026 capex stays $60-64B as far as reported (Q3 spend $13.84B, $40.64B year to date), which is direct evidence that AI accelerator volumes (and so HBM demand) are still rising. Consensus target $252.21 (15 analysts, Strong Buy), 71% upside. Status and conviction unchanged: the falls are market-wide and about China competition and rates; no change to HBM orders or guidance has been reported.
risks: CXMT closing the density gap would pressure DRAM pricing from 2027, and the market is pricing that. Korean selling is now forced and mechanical (two circuit-breaker days for the KOSPI in a week, a seven-session losing streak), so the ADR can gap lower again Thursday US time. The buyback is about 90% done and due to end around Oct 20. Solidigm's capital plan is undecided. Holding buy/high through this needs Q3 results to confirm HBM pricing.
catalyst: ADR reaction to Seoul's -11% Thu Oct 15 (US open 00:30 AEDT Fri); buyback ends ~Oct 20; Q3 results expected around Oct 28 KST (not yet posted by the company); Samsung full Q3 results Oct 29.

name: Bloom Energy
thesis: Bloom Energy makes solid-oxide fuel cells for onsite data-centre power; Q2 revenue was a record $1.07B and FY26 guidance is $3.9-4.2B, anchored by Oracle (up to 2.8 GW) and Brookfield ($25B). Wednesday Oct 14 it fell 9.15% to $239.34, from an intraday high of $258.52, as rising yields after hot CPI hit high-multiple power names; no company news found. Bloom confirmed on Oct 12 that Q3 results come Oct 22 after the US close, earlier than the Oct 27 estimate. Consensus target $284.74 (29 analysts, Buy) is now 19% above the price; UBS $350, Bernstein Hold $282.
risks: Upside rests on Oracle and Brookfield deployments converting to revenue on schedule. It moves 6-9% on AI-capex and rate headlines without company news (Oct 8, Oct 12, Oct 14). Q3 consensus EPS is a thin $0.14; a margin miss would hit a stock that has doubled this year, and the report is now a week away.
catalyst: Q3 results Thu Oct 22 after US close, call 5:00pm ET (08:00 AEDT Fri Oct 23), confirmed by Bloom Oct 12; Oracle Jupiter permit Nov 23.

name: GE Vernova
thesis: GE Vernova builds gas turbines, grid equipment and wind for the power build-out; Q2 revenue was $11.1B (+22% y/y) with gas capacity largely contracted through 2030. Wednesday Oct 14 it fell 6.20% to $941.78, back below $1,000, after an intraday low of $922.24; no company news found - the move came with the CPI-driven selloff in AI-power names (Vertiv -6.1%, Bloom -9.2%). JPMorgan cut its target to $1,150 from $1,330 on Oct 9, keeping Overweight. Consensus target $1,225 (37 analysts, Buy), 30% upside.
risks: Q2 EPS of $2.47 missed the $3.17 consensus and wind keeps losing money, so another margin miss on Oct 28 would test the premium multiple; JPMorgan's cut is the second target trim in three weeks after Jefferies. GLJ has a $470 Sell. Higher-for-longer rates (10-year above 5.2%) raise the cost of the utility and data-centre projects that buy its turbines.
catalyst: Q3 results Oct 28, webcast 7:30-8:30am ET (22:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28).

name: Vertiv
thesis: Vertiv sells power, thermal and liquid-cooling gear for data centres; Q2 sales were $3.27B (+24%) and it guided Q3 to $3.65-3.85B and EPS $1.77-1.83, lifting FY26 EPS to $6.65-6.75. Wednesday Oct 14 it fell 6.09% to $222.83, a fifth straight decline, in the CPI-driven AI-infrastructure selloff; no company news found. TSMC (Oct 15) beat on Q3 (revenue $46.72B vs a $44.6-45.8B guide, HPC 68% of revenue, +22% q/q) and guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B vs about $48.8B expected; 2026 capex stays $60-64B as far as reported (Q3 spend $13.84B, $40.64B year to date), which points to more AI racks to power and cool in Q4. Consensus target $337.43 (30 analysts, Strong Buy), 51% upside. Q3 date still not announced as of this run.
risks: GLJ's $188 Sell case is that hyperscaler capex slows in 2027, and the stock trades on that debate rather than on guidance; it is now 18.5% above that target. Q3 consensus EPS of $1.57 sits below the company's own $1.77-1.83 range, so the bar is low, but any order-timing slip would be punished. Price competition in liquid cooling is rising.
catalyst: Q3 results expected Oct 21 or Oct 28 (company has not announced; last quarter's notice came 14 days ahead).

name: Robinhood
thesis: Robinhood is a retail brokerage adding prediction markets, perpetual futures, earnings contracts and Robinhood Agents (announced Sep 29); Q2 revenue was $1.31B (+32%), net income $561M. August data (released Sep 10): 28.6M funded customers, $384B platform assets (+8% m/m), $4.0B net deposits, equity volume $335B (+68% y/y). Wednesday Oct 14 it fell 8.54% to $101.08, ending a three-day gain, on a day high-multiple growth names sold off after hot CPI; no company news found. September operating data had not been released at this run. Consensus target $134.68 (30 analysts, Buy), 33% upside; Morgan Stanley $160 (Oct 9).
risks: Revenue tracks crypto and equity volumes, so a bitcoin drawdown or a quieter October shows up fast in the monthly metrics; crypto revenue already fell in Q2. Its 8.5% drop on a macro day shows how rate-sensitive the multiple is. Prediction markets are a new line with routing and regulatory dependencies. Wells Fargo started at Hold ($125) on Oct 1.
catalyst: September operating data due mid-October (not yet out at 18:00 AEDT Oct 15); shareholder Q&A on Say opens Oct 20; Q3 results Oct 27 after close, video call 5pm ET (08:00 AEDT Wed Oct 28).

name: MercadoLibre
thesis: MercadoLibre runs Latin America's largest marketplace, logistics network and the Mercado Pago fintech; Q2 net revenue was $10.2B (+50% y/y), GMV $21.9B (+44%), TPV $101B (+56%), with operating income down 17% to $683M. The stock is riding Brazil's election: Flavio Bolsonaro leads Lula 52-48 in valid votes in Datafolha (Oct 8) and 52.8-47.2 in AtlasIntel/Bloomberg (Oct 9). Wednesday Oct 14 it fell 1.97% to $1,839.11, a third straight decline but a small one next to the AI names; no company news found. Consensus target $2,276 (26 analysts, Buy), 24% upside.
risks: The Oct 25 runoff is not decided: Datafolha's lead is within its 2-point margin, and a Lula win would unwind much of the post-vote gain. Margins are compressing as the $16B credit book (+75% y/y) and logistics build-out absorb revenue growth; Q2 profit fell while sales rose 50%. Higher US rates tend to pull money out of Brazilian assets. Earnings move the stock sharply (-8.3% after Q2).
catalyst: Brazil runoff Sun Oct 25 (results Mon Oct 26 morning AEDT); Q3 results Nov 4 (provisional per IR calendar).

name: Cloudflare
thesis: Cloudflare runs a global edge network selling security, CDN, zero-trust and the Workers developer platform; trailing revenue is $2.51B, up 33.5%. Wednesday Oct 14 it fell 6.72% to $324.33, a third down day that leaves it about 7% below last Friday's 52-week-high close; no company news found - software sold off with chips after hot CPI. The price is back below the $341 mean target (34 analysts, Buy), 5% upside; BTIG $413 and Oppenheimer $430 imply 27-33%. Q3 results listed for Oct 29 (estimated, not yet confirmed by the company).
risks: Still up sharply this year, so the Q3 print has to beat and raise. The stock has had 38 moves of more than 5% in the past year; any wobble in Workers or AI-related monetisation would hit hard. Long-duration software multiples are the first to compress when yields rise, as they did Oct 14.
catalyst: Q3 results ~Oct 29 (TBC). This is the pullback the earlier note said to wait for; adding into the print is a judgement call on rates.

name: Sea Limited
thesis: Sea runs Shopee (e-commerce), SeaMoney (digital finance) and Garena (games) across Southeast Asia and Brazil; trailing revenue is $27.7B, up 43.1%. Wednesday Oct 14 it slipped 0.65% to $95.31, barely touched by the AI selloff, with no company news found. Forward PE is 22 against 40%+ revenue growth, market cap $58B. Mean target $154.93 (29 analysts, Strong Buy) implies 63% upside; DBS Hold $105 and Arete Buy $152 bracket the range.
risks: Q2 EPS missed and the stock has drifted for a year; the market wants margin proof from Shopee as it fights TikTok Shop and Temu. Currency and credit-quality risk in the Brazil and Indonesia lending book. No company news Oct 13-15; thesis and status unchanged.

name: BYD
thesis: BYD is the largest NEV maker with in-house batteries and chips and a growing export push; September sales were 463,561 (+17%). Hong Kong closed Wednesday Oct 14 at HK$72.85 (-0.55%) and was HK$72.65 (-0.27%, about US$9.26 at 7.848 HKD/USD) at 14:47 HKT Thursday, intraday with the close at 16:00 HKT (19:00 AEDT); Thursday's low was HK$71.80, 0.6% above the HK$71.40 52-week low. The Da Han flagship EV launched Oct 13 at 235,900-275,900 yuan, up to 24,000 yuan below its pre-sale prices. JPMorgan Neutral HK$88 implies 21% upside. Weekly China registrations for Oct 5-11 were not found at this run.
risks: The domestic price war keeps margins under pressure: the Da Han launched up to 24,000 yuan below its own pre-sale prices. The Oct 12 China-EU deal curbs Chinese hybrid exports ('several million cars over four years' per the EU; caps and price floors still being negotiated, no new details found Oct 14-15); BYD is the largest Chinese hybrid exporter to Europe. A close below HK$71.40 would be the signal to step back, and Thursday's low came within HK$0.40 of it. Thursday's figure is intraday, not the final close.
catalyst: Paris Motor Show to Oct 18; weekly China registrations (Oct 5-11 data not yet found); EU hybrid-cap implementation rules (no date); China Q3 GDP and activity data Mon Oct 19, 13:00 AEDT; Q3 results late October.

name: Keyence
thesis: Keyence sells machine-vision, sensors and measurement gear direct to factories with industry-leading margins and no debt; trailing revenue is JPY 1.25T, up 16.9%. Thursday Oct 15 it closed at JPY 78,970 (-1.69%, about US$499 at 158.31 JPY/USD), after an intraday low of JPY 77,380, as Asian tech sold off after hot US CPI; no company news found. Mean target of JPY 97,867 (15 analysts, Strong Buy) implies 24% upside. Fiscal Q2 results listed for Oct 29 (StockAnalysis; treat as TBC).
risks: Capex-cycle sensitivity: a slowdown in China or US factory automation shows up in orders within a quarter. A stronger yen cuts reported overseas revenue. Tokyo-only listing with no ADR, so execution is harder for an Australian buyer. No company news found Oct 13-15; status unchanged - Thursday's fall was market-wide.

name: ASML Holding
thesis: ASML is the only supplier of EUV lithography tools for leading-edge chips. Q3 2026 (Oct 14): net sales EUR 11.66B (record; a touch under the EUR 11.72B consensus), gross margin 57.5% (guide 55-57%), net income EUR 4.96B, EPS EUR 12.95; Q4 guide EUR 14.2-15.2B at about 57%, lifting 2026 to EUR 44-45B. CEO Fouquet: planned supply for 2027 and 2028 'will not fully meet the demand of our customers'. Market reaction split: Amsterdam recovered from an early drop to close Wednesday at EUR 1,528.20 (+1.23%), but the ADR fell 3.94% to $1,650.00 in the US CPI selloff (semis ETF SMH about -4%). TSMC, ASML's largest EUV customer, then beat on Q3 and guided Q4 revenue to $52.3-54.3B vs about $48.8B expected, keeping 2026 capex at $60-64B as far as reported. Mean target $2,099 (42 analysts, Strong Buy), 27% upside. Status kept at buy/high: the results and TSMC's guide both support demand; the ADR drop tracked the market, not the print.
risks: Revenue was only in line, and expectations for a multi-year EUV cycle are high. China was put at about 20% of the business on the call and export rules can change. Memory customers (SK hynix, Samsung) fell 10-11% again in Seoul Thursday on CXMT and rate worries. Supply, not demand, now caps growth: any slip in the 30% capacity build would cap 2027-28 sales. Q4 needs a 26% step-up in sales from Q3. Amsterdam trades Thursday after the ADR's fall, so expect a lower open.
catalyst: Amsterdam reaction Thu Oct 15 (opens 18:00 AEDT) to the ADR drop and TSMC's guide; Lam Research Oct 21 (08:00 AEDT Thu Oct 22); interim dividend EUR 1.88 payable Nov 4; Q4 results January (date TBC).

name: Teradyne
thesis: Teradyne makes automated test equipment for AI accelerators, HBM memory and mobile chips, plus a robotics arm (Universal Robots, MiR); trailing revenue is $4.46B, up 57.9%. Wednesday Oct 14 it fell 5.48% to $359.44; it is 20.0% below the Oct 2 close of $449.04 and has fallen seven of the last eight sessions. No company news found. TSMC (Oct 15) beat on Q3 (revenue $46.72B vs a $44.6-45.8B guide, HPC 68% of revenue, +22% q/q) and guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B vs about $48.8B expected; 2026 capex stays $60-64B as far as reported (Q3 spend $13.84B, $40.64B year to date); 2nm rose to 8% of TSMC wafer revenue from 3% in Q2, and each new node adds test time. Mean target $446.47 (17 analysts, Buy) implies 24% upside; Baird's $420 Neutral is 17% above the price.
risks: HBM test demand is a large part of the story, so the memory selloff (SK hynix -11% in Seoul Thursday) hits Teradyne directly. Test spend is lumpy and concentrated in a few AI customers. Robotics growth has lagged. The pullback makes the entry more interesting but does not change the status until Q3 shows memory-test orders holding.
catalyst: IEEE ITC to Oct 16; Lam Research Oct 21 (08:00 AEDT Thu Oct 22); Q3 results ~Oct 27 (TBC).

name: Tesla
thesis: Tesla sells EVs and storage and is pivoting the story to robotaxi (Cybercab) and Optimus; trailing revenue is $103.6B, up 11.8%. Wednesday Oct 14 it fell 2.15% to $367.16, a third straight decline, with no company news found. Tesla's 8-K confirms Q3 results after the close on Wed Oct 21 with a Q&A webcast at 5:30pm ET (08:30 AEDT Thu Oct 22). The Cybercab is on show at the Paris Motor Show (to Oct 18). Mean target $396.57 (44 analysts) implies 8% upside. The Roadster demo date (Oct 15 per the Sep 28 reschedule) could not be reconfirmed; Electrek counts at least eight delays since 2017.
risks: Europe is getting harder: Tesla dropped the 'Full Self-Driving' name there after German pushback (Oct 9) and an EU-wide FSD decision is expected in December. Q2 EPS of $0.33 missed the $0.50 estimate, and at about 200x forward earnings a Q3 miss or soft Cybercab ramp commentary leaves little cushion. Product events have a history of 'sell the news' reactions. Status unchanged.
catalyst: Roadster demo Oct 15 (Fri morning AEDT; not reconfirmed); Paris Motor Show to Oct 18; Q3 results Wed Oct 21 after close, Q&A 5:30pm ET (08:30 AEDT Thu Oct 22), confirmed by 8-K; EU FSD decision expected December.
